extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers (potential Ambizione applicants), research administrators, Swiss research community
extracted.subtask_description: Information about the SNSF Ambizione funding scheme for promising young researchers, including who may apply, the evaluation process, funding amounts and project duration, and gender-balance target. Useful for prospective applicants and stakeholders tracking outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — target applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 2008, the SNSF has launched Ambizione calls to promote promising young researchers from Switzerland and abroad. Scientific staff at higher education institutions can also apply for Ambizione grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be promising young researchers (from Switzerland or abroad); scientific staff at higher education institutions are explicitly eligible. Projects must be conducted and managed at a higher education institution or other institution in Switzerland.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career stage requirement — first independent project
rubrics_metrics.description: Thanks to their Ambizione grant, the 84 researchers will be able to conduct and manage their first independent project at a higher education institution or other institution in Switzerland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scheme is intended to support researchers taking their first step into running an independent research project; proposals should be for a first independent project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation process — two-step selection and rating-based funding
rubrics_metrics.description: In November 2020, a record number of 480 young researchers submitted an Ambizione application. 144 applicants reached the second phase of the evaluation process. Following this two-step evaluation, the SNSF awarded 84 new grants. The highest rated of 480 submitted projects will be funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is by a multi-stage (two-step) evaluation with projects scored/rated; advancement to phase two is selective and final funding is awarded to the highest-rated applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender-balance target
rubrics_metrics.description: With 24 grants going to women (28.4%), unfortunately the targeted share of 35% female awardees was not achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SNSF has an explicit target share for female awardees (35%); gender balance is a stated goal that informs outcomes and monitoring, though page does not specify whether it is a formal selection criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding quantum and typical award size
rubrics_metrics.description: On average, they will receive 766,000 francs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should plan projects and budgets consistent with an average grant of around CHF 766,000; page implies multi-year funding sufficient to run an independent project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project duration and start date
rubrics_metrics.description: Most of the projects will start in autumn 2021 and run for four years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful proposals are typically funded for a four-year period and should be planned with that timeframe and likely autumn start in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary coverage — wide range of topics accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the approved projects, 43% are in mathematics, the natural sciences and engineering, 38% in the humanities and social sciences, and 19% in biology and medicine. This distribution is reflected in the wide range of topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambizione supports a broad range of disciplines across humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, engineering, biology and medicine; applicants from any of these fields may be considered.
